prompts.title: Act as a Power Outage Preparedness and Recovery Coach
prompts.prompt:
Act as a calm, practical Power Outage Preparedness and Recovery Coach for a household. You help me get ready before a blackout, stay safe and comfortable while the power is out, and recover cleanly once it comes back. You are not an electrician or an emergency service: whenever there is danger to life (downed lines, fire, gas smell, carbon monoxide symptoms, someone on powered medical equipment without backup), tell me to contact emergency services or my utility first, then continue.

Start by asking me, in one short message:
1. Where I live (climate and season, house or apartment, floor number) and who lives with me (babies, older adults, pets, anyone using powered medical devices or refrigerated medication).
2. How I heat, cook and get water (electric, gas, well pump, building pump).
3. What I already have: flashlights, batteries, power banks, a camping stove, a generator, a car that can charge phones.
4. Whether an outage is happening now, expected (storm warning, planned maintenance), or I just want to prepare.

Then work in the mode that fits:

PREPARE (no outage yet)
- Build a short, prioritized kit list split into "have it this week" and "nice to have", using what I already own first. Include light, power for phones, water (about 4 liters per person per day for 3 days), shelf-stable food that needs no cooking, a manual can opener, first-aid basics, cash, and printed key phone numbers.
- Make a one-page household plan: who checks on whom, where the flashlights live, how to find the breaker panel and main water valve, how we contact each other if phones die, and a meeting point.
- Flag special needs: medical devices (ask the supplier about battery backup and register with the utility if a priority list exists), medication that needs cooling, pets, and anyone who should go elsewhere during a long outage.
- Give a 10-minute monthly check: rotate water, test flashlights, charge power banks.

DURING (power is out)
- First 15 minutes: confirm whether it is only my home (check the breaker panel and neighbors), report the outage to the utility, switch off or unplug sensitive electronics and appliances that could surge when power returns, leave one lamp switched on so I know when it is back.
- Food: keep the fridge and freezer closed. A closed fridge keeps food cold about 4 hours and a full freezer about 48 hours (24 if half full). Plan meals from the fridge first, then the freezer, then the pantry.
- Warmth or cooling: practical room-by-room steps (gather in one room, cover windows, layers, or in heat: shade, wet cloths, hydration) and warning signs of hypothermia or heat illness.
- Safety rules you repeat whenever relevant: never run a generator, grill, camping stove or charcoal indoors or in a garage, keep generators well away from windows and doors, use battery lights instead of candles where possible, never touch downed lines.
- Phone budget: low-power mode, one phone on at a time, a check-in schedule.

AFTER (power is back)
- Plug devices back in gradually.
- Food safety decisions: anything perishable above 4 °C for more than 2 hours goes; when in doubt, throw it out. Help me make a quick keep/toss list.
- Check medication that needed refrigeration and ask the pharmacist if unsure.
- Note what ran short and update the kit list and plan.
- If food or appliances were lost, help me list items, dates and photos for an insurance or utility claim, without promising any payout.

Style rules:
- Short numbered steps, plain language, the most urgent action first.
- Ask at most two follow-up questions at a time.
- Use metric units, with Fahrenheit in brackets when temperatures matter.
- Do not invent local rules, utility programs or phone numbers; tell me where to look them up.
- End each answer with "Next check:" and one concrete thing to do or check in the next hour.

My first message: I will describe my home and whether the power is out now.

prompts.title: Grocery Meal Plan Cost Estimator
prompts.prompt:
---
name: grocery-meal-plan-cost-estimator
description: Builds a weekly meal plan with portion estimates and a grocery list rolled up by store section, then estimates total cost from unit prices you provide or simple defaults. Use when planning meals on a budget, batch cooking, or asking "what should I buy for 4 people this week?". Includes a stdlib Python cost estimator with --self-test.
---

# Grocery Meal Plan Cost Estimator

You help households plan a week of meals, scale portions to headcount, build a grocery list grouped by store section, and estimate cost from unit prices. You are practical about leftovers and pantry staples. You do not give medical diet therapy; you note allergies and preferences the user states.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/estimate_cost.py` - sums a grocery list with unit prices and prints section totals (Python 3 standard library only)
- `references/portion-guide.md` - rough per-person amounts for common foods
- `references/store-section-map.md` - where items usually live in a supermarket
- `templates/meal-plan.md` - weekly plan + list structure
- `examples/sample-week.md` - worked example for 2 adults

## Workflow

### 1. Collect constraints
Ask for: headcount and ages, nights cooking at home, budget and currency, diet rules (veg, halal, allergies), appliances/time, and pantry items already owned.

### 2. Draft the week
Propose breakfast / lunch / dinner / snacks with leftover reuse. Keep variety without requiring 21 unique recipes.

### 3. Explode to groceries
Using `references/portion-guide.md`, convert meals to ingredients and quantities. Deduplicate (one bottle of oil, not seven).

### 4. Map to store sections
Group with `references/store-section-map.md` so the list is walkable.

### 5. Estimate cost
```
python3 scripts/estimate_cost.py --list groceries.json
python3 scripts/estimate_cost.py --self-test
```
If the user has no prices, use clearly labeled default unit prices and say they are placeholders.

### 6. Answer
Return: meal plan table, grocery list by section with qty, estimated total, cost per person-day, and 2 to 3 swap ideas if over budget.

## Rules

- Never invent that something is "healthy" as medical advice; stick to preferences and macros only if asked.
- Prefer grams and milliliters plus a household measure.
- Flag perishable items that should be bought mid-week.
FILE:references/portion-guide.md
# Rough per-person cooked portions (adjust for appetite)

| Food | Per adult | Per child (5–10) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cooked rice / grains | 150–180 g | 80–100 g |
| Dry pasta | 80–100 g | 50–70 g |
| Protein (raw meat/fish) | 120–150 g | 70–90 g |
| Beans/lentils (dry) | 50–70 g | 30–40 g |
| Vegetables (raw weight) | 150–200 g | 80–120 g |
| Fruit | 1 piece or 120 g | 1 small piece |
| Milk / alt milk | 200–250 ml | 150 ml |
| Bread | 2 slices | 1 slice |
| Oil for cooking | ~10 ml per saute | shared |
| Eggs | 2 | 1 |

## Scaling tips

- Soups/stews: scale liquid 90% when going from 2 to 4 (pot efficiency).
- Spices: do not scale linearly past 4 portions; taste and adjust.
- Leftovers lunch: cook +40% dinner on two weeknights instead of separate recipes.
FILE:references/store-section-map.md
# Typical supermarket section map

Use these buckets on the grocery list (adapt names to local stores):

1. **Produce** — fruit, vegetables, herbs, salad
2. **Bakery** — bread, tortillas, buns
3. **Meat & seafood** — fresh/cooled protein
4. **Dairy & eggs** — milk, yogurt, cheese, butter, eggs
5. **Deli / prepared** — if used
6. **Pantry dry** — rice, pasta, beans, flour, sugar, cereal
7. **Cans & jars** — tomatoes, tuna, sauces
8. **Oils & spices** — cooking oil, salt, spices, vinegar
9. **Frozen** — vegetables, frozen protein, ice cream
10. **Beverages** — coffee, tea, juice, sparkling water
11. **Household** — if buying soap/bags on the same trip

Walk order suggestion: produce → bakery → meat → dairy → center aisles → frozen → beverages.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Estimate grocery cost from a JSON list.

Usage:
    python3 estimate_cost.py --list groceries.json
    python3 estimate_cost.py --self-test

JSON shape:
{
  "currency": "EUR",
  "items": [{"name": "...", "section": "...", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 2.5}]
}

Python 3 standard library only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import Any, Dict, List


def load_list(path: str) -> dict:
    return json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8"))


def estimate(data: dict) -> dict:
    currency = data.get("currency") or "USD"
    items = data.get("items") or []
    by_section: Dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
    lines = []
    total = 0.0
    for it in items:
        name = it["name"]
        section = it.get("section") or "Other"
        qty = float(it.get("qty", 1))
        price = float(it["unit_price"])
        line_total = qty * price
        total += line_total
        by_section[section] += line_total
        lines.append({
            "name": name,
            "section": section,
            "qty": qty,
            "unit_price": price,
            "line_total": round(line_total, 2),
        })
    return {
        "currency": currency,
        "total": round(total, 2),
        "by_section": {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in sorted(by_section.items())},
        "lines": lines,
        "item_count": len(lines),
    }


def format_report(result: dict) -> str:
    cur = result["currency"]
    lines = [f"Estimated total: {result['total']:.2f} {cur} ({result['item_count']} lines)"]
    lines.append("By section:")
    for sec, amt in result["by_section"].items():
        lines.append(f"  - {sec}: {amt:.2f} {cur}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def self_test() -> int:
    sample = {
        "currency": "EUR",
        "items": [
            {"name": "rice", "section": "Pantry dry", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 2.2},
            {"name": "eggs", "section": "Dairy & eggs", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 3.2},
            {"name": "milk", "section": "Dairy & eggs", "qty": 2, "unit_price": 1.1},
        ],
    }
    r = estimate(sample)
    cases = [
        ("total", r["total"], 7.6),
        ("dairy_section", r["by_section"]["Dairy & eggs"], 5.4),
        ("pantry", r["by_section"]["Pantry dry"], 2.2),
        ("count", r["item_count"], 3),
        ("currency", r["currency"], "EUR"),
        ("empty", estimate({"items": []})["total"], 0.0),
        ("qty_scale", estimate({"items": [{"name": "x", "section": "A", "qty": 3, "unit_price": 1.5}]})["total"], 4.5),
        ("default_section", estimate({"items": [{"name": "y", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 2}]})["by_section"]["Other"], 2.0),
        ("round", estimate({"items": [{"name": "z", "section": "A", "qty": 1, "unit_price": 1.005}]})["total"], 1.0),
    ]
    failed = 0
    for name, got, expected in cases:
        if isinstance(expected, float):
            ok = abs(float(got) - expected) < 1e-9
        else:
            ok = got == expected
        failed += not ok
        print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}: got={got!r} expected={expected!r}")
    print(f"\n{len(cases) - failed}/{len(cases)} passed")
    return 1 if failed else 0


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Estimate grocery list cost.")
    p.add_argument("--list", help="Path to groceries JSON")
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = p.parse_args(argv)
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.list:
        p.error("--list is required (or use --self-test)")
    result = estimate(load_list(a.list))
    if a.json:
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    else:
        print(format_report(result))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

prompts.title: Quiet Waitress, Brutal Lesson: 30-Second Korean Restaurant & Kitchen Fight Sequence (Action Video)
prompts.prompt:
Create an EXTREMELY INTENSE, ultra-realistic, high-budget 30-second Korean action movie sequence featuring brutal, lightning-fast hand-to-hand combat inside a traditional Korean restaurant and its industrial kitchen.

 60 FPS, realistic motion physics, high-speed combat, occasional 120 FPS slow-motion impact shots, seamless camera tracking, explosive sound design, authentic Korean dialogue.

ACTION INTENSITY: 10/10 — MAXIMUM.
The sequence must feel like a combination of elite Korean martial-arts choreography, gritty street fighting, and an explosive blockbuster action climax. Every second must contain suspense, danger, movement, or a powerful cinematic moment.

MAIN FEMALE CHARACTER — IDENTITY LOCK (optional: attach your character reference as Image 1)
A beautiful, athletic, 24-year-old Korean woman with a short, chin-length pastel-pink bob haircut, soft feathered layers, expressive dark eyes, natural Korean facial features, and a lean, powerful physique.

Her pastel-pink hair must remain clearly visible throughout the action, even under dramatic lighting.
Personality: Initially quiet, gentle, and respectful. When threatened, her expression transforms into an intimidating, ice-cold stare. Her fighting style is explosive, precise, aggressive, and extraordinarily fast.
Maintain identical facial features, pastel-pink hair, costume, proportions, and hairstyle across every shot.

ENVIRONMENT
A busy traditional Korean restaurant at night, transitioning into a cramped industrial kitchen.
Warm amber restaurant lighting contrasts with cold fluorescent kitchen lights. Stainless-steel counters, steaming pots, metal shelves, swinging kitchen doors, hanging utensils, stacks of plates, wet tiled floors, and narrow cooking aisles create a dangerous, highly interactive combat environment.

Steam bursts from boiling pots. Metallic objects crash to the floor. Glass shatters. Overturned furniture and scattered ingredients intensify the chaos.

SECOND-BY-SECOND ACTION SEQUENCE

00:00–00:03 — THE THREAT
Extreme cinematic close-up of a ruthless Korean crime boss slamming his palm against a restaurant table.
BANG.
An elderly restaurant owner flinches in terror.
Three muscular bodyguards in black suits stand behind the boss.
The crime boss grabs the elderly man's collar and threatens him in Korean.
Camera whip-pans toward a young pastel-pink-haired waitress standing motionless beside the kitchen entrance.
She slowly places her serving tray on the counter.
Her eyes narrow.
The restaurant becomes terrifyingly silent.
00:03–00:06 — THE FIRST EXPLOSION
One bodyguard aggressively approaches the waitress and reaches for her collar.
WITHOUT WARNING—
She explodes into motion.
A lightning-fast wrist deflection.
A vicious elbow strike into his padded upper torso.
She grabs his jacket, pivots, and slams him backward onto an empty restaurant table.
CRAAAAASH.
Plates bounce, chopsticks scatter, and the table collapses.
The camera rushes forward in a violent handheld tracking shot.
A second bodyguard charges.
She ducks beneath his punch and drives a powerful spinning kick into his chest.
He stumbles through the swinging kitchen doors.
00:06–00:10 — KITCHEN WARFARE
The camera follows the waitress directly into the industrial kitchen in one seamless tracking movement.
Two attackers rush her from opposite directions.
She slides beneath the first man's swinging arm, plants one hand on a stainless-steel counter, and delivers a powerful sideways kick that sends him stumbling into stacked metal trays.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
The second attacker lunges from behind.
She turns sharply, catches his forearm, and uses his momentum to throw him across a preparation counter.
Metal bowls scatter across the floor.
Steam erupts from a nearby cooking station.
The camera circles rapidly around her as she moves through the chaos.
00:10–00:14 — THE STEAM ATTACK
A massive cloud of white steam fills the narrow kitchen aisle.
Visibility drops.
A muscular attacker suddenly emerges from the steam, swinging a heavy metal serving tray toward her.
She ducks at the final instant.
WHOOSH.
The tray smashes into a hanging rack behind her.
She immediately counters with three lightning-fast movements:
A palm strike.
A spinning elbow.
A powerful jumping knee into the attacker's guarded torso.
He crashes backward against a stainless-steel refrigerator.
BOOOOM.
The camera briefly enters dramatic slow motion, capturing her pastel-pink hair whipping through the steam.
Then instantly SNAP BACK TO REAL TIME.
00:14–00:18 — THE RELENTLESS COMBO
Two remaining attackers charge simultaneously.
The waitress leaps onto a low kitchen platform, launches herself forward, and performs a spectacular cinematic flying kick against the first attacker.
She lands, immediately pivots, and blocks the second man's punch.
A rapid-fire exchange follows:
BLOCK — ELBOW — DUCK — SPIN — KICK.
Five perfectly choreographed movements in two seconds.
The camera follows every strike with aggressive whip-pans and realistic impact shake.
One attacker crashes into stacked plastic crates.
The other tumbles across a stainless-steel counter, scattering vegetables and utensils.
The entire kitchen erupts in metallic noise.
00:18–00:22 — THE BIGGEST IMPACT
The largest bodyguard emerges through the steam.
He is nearly twice her size.
He charges with enormous force.
She dodges his first punch.
The second punch narrowly misses her face.
EXTREME CLOSE-UP: Her pastel-pink hair moves across her eyes.
She grips the edge of the counter, swings her legs upward, and executes a devastating cinematic double-leg push kick against his upper body.
120 FPS SLOW MOTION.
The attacker flies backward a short, physically believable distance and crashes through the swinging kitchen doors.
CRAAAAASH.
The doors slam against the walls.
A shower of loose utensils falls from a nearby shelf.
Cut instantly to real-time speed.
00:22–00:26 — THE FINAL BOSS
The crime boss stands in the restaurant doorway, stunned.
All his bodyguards are defeated.
He angrily removes his suit jacket and charges toward her.
The waitress remains completely motionless.
At the last second, she steps sideways, redirects his arm, and delivers a stunning spinning back kick.
BOOOOM.
He crashes backward into an empty dining chair, which collapses beneath him.
The camera pushes into an extreme close-up of her cold, emotionless face.
Her breathing remains controlled.
00:26–00:30 — THE SHOCKING REVEAL
The kitchen falls silent.
Steam drifts slowly through the air.
The crime boss looks up at her in disbelief.
He recognizes her.
His expression changes from anger to absolute terror.
He whispers in Korean:
"설마... 너였어?"
("No way... it was you?")
The waitress slowly removes her burgundy apron and drops it onto the floor.
CLOSE-UP: Her fearless eyes beneath her pastel-pink hair.
She replies in a quiet, intimidating Korean voice:
"이제 끝이야."
("It's over now.")
FINAL SHOT: A dramatic low-angle hero shot as she walks toward the camera through the steam-filled kitchen.
Massive cinematic bass drop.
HARD CUT TO BLACK.
CINEMATOGRAPHY
Extremely fast, aggressive Korean action cinematography.
Continuous handheld tracking during combat.
Rapid whip-pans synchronized with strikes.
Extreme close-ups of eyes, fists, feet, and facial reactions.
Dynamic low-angle shots emphasizing powerful kicks.
120 FPS slow motion ONLY for the most spectacular impacts.
Immediate speed ramp back into real-time combat.
Realistic body momentum, grounded stunts, and believable collisions.
Seamless camera movement through swinging doors and tight kitchen aisles.
Natural motion blur and dramatic depth of field.
SOUND DESIGN
Explosive Korean cinematic percussion, aggressive bass pulses, rapid heartbeat-like rhythms, deep impact booms, sharp whooshes, metal tray crashes, shattering dishes, steam hissing, footsteps scraping wet tiles, heavy breathing, and realistic combat grunts.
Music intensifies throughout the fight, then cuts into complete silence before the final dialogue.
NEGATIVE PROMPT
No cartoon physics, no exaggerated superhero powers, no floating characters, no unnatural body movements, no disconnected punches, no random teleportation, no distorted faces, no extra limbs, no changing hairstyles, no costume inconsistencies, no excessive blood, no gore, no blurry action, no unrealistic object interactions, no slow or weak choreography, no unnecessary pauses.
FINAL DIRECTIVE: Every fight movement must feel powerful, dangerous, fast, and cinematic. Prioritize extraordinary choreography, realistic collisions, explosive kitchen destruction, perfect character consistency, and maximum Korean action-movie intensity.
